Perfume rating 4.00 out of 5 with 6,971 votes

Perles De Lalique by Lalique is a Chypre Floral fragrance for women. Perles De Lalique was launched in 2006. The nose behind this fragrance is Nathalie Lorson. Top note is Rose; middle notes are Pepper, Iris and Powdery Notes; base notes are Patchouli, Oakmoss, Vetiver, Orris Root and Cashmirwood.

This perfume was introduced in 2006. It won a best-perfume award in 2007 by Marie Claire. There are two kinds of bottle; one was designed especially as an extrait de parfum 60ml bottle and the other as Eau de Toilette 50ml and 100ml bottle. The extrait de parfum bottle was inspired by by the René Lalique “Cactus” powder bowl of 1928, which is the real symbol of femininity. The flacon is handmade, made of opal with a beautiful stopper adorned by black dots.Every single bottle is signed and has its own unique number. This chypre-floral compositon was designed by Nathalie Lorson, Firmenich. The notes are voluptuous, intoxicating, feminine and very seductive. Bulgarin rose shines with its sweet and spicy nuances. At its heart, the note of sensual and powdery iris caressed by bourbon pepper which offers the wave of some modern colouring seguing into patchouli and musks. The casmir note gives off its elegant and refined character.

LOST_HORIZON 12/04/25 14:33

Perles de Lalique is a patchouli and rose perfume with a slightly camphoraceous note. It's so decadent; even though the bottle is white, it feels incredibly gothic, nocturnal, and eerie. I feel like it could be the perfume of a spirit, one of those white ladies you see in cemeteries by moonlight that send shivers down your spine... It's a dark, poetic fragrance, like reading Edgar Allan Poe in the cold winter. Very interesting; if you know when to wear it, you won't be disappointed.

This is nice. I wear it as an ankle perfume bc if it were too close to my nose I’d start to become annoyed. It’s powdery and sharp. I blind bought this based on reviews, but i have some bones to pick. I will start off by saying it wasn't a fail, i actually like this fragrance. There is nothin camphorous, or gothic about this fragrance however. You could fool me into thinking this was a designer 90s perfume. The comparisons to Dior Midnight Poison are accurate. The profile shows woody, earthy at the top of the pyramid and again i disagree. I LOVE woody, earthy fragrances and would not say those are the top profiles here. Rose should be at the top. This opens with a medicinal, almost licorice type rose, almost identical to the opening of 1969-Histoires de Parfums. I guess that might be what people refer to as camphorous, but to me it is more of a cherry syrup type medicine, instead of a tiger balm medicine (which is what i would describe as camphor). The dry down is sweet. I get absolutely no wood in this. I get the patchouli. To me it is a straighforward rose fruity patchouli. Very nice, but not at all haunted, or gothic as many suggest. It is "dark" in the sense that this profile is probably better worn at night, but other than that i think it's very pretty. I would wear this in the winter because this type of sweet, rose-patchouli is best suited for that season in my opinion.

Hirvdinia 07/09/25 16:21

As someone very new to the world of fragrances, this is a wonderful scent. My first blind pick (and only second perfume I've owned, admittedly) all of the notes listed had me very interested, and fairly confident I would, at the very least, not dislike it. I was correct, it smells lovely. From the perspective of someone unfamiliar with distinguishing notes, it is a woody scent with a light and feminine air to it. I believe the main note I'm getting is the vetiver, as it reminds me a lot of my oils and some of the more common incense sticks I've smelled.

I do not pick up on the iris or the rose, however I'm assuming those notes are there to soften the base notes rather than compete with them. My family agreed they mostly get a wood-based essential oil smell. With this in mind it is still a great perfume, but if anyone has a recommendation for a similar perfume with more emphasis on a powdery scent, please let me know!

As far as negatives, this is hard to discern for me at the moment due to my inexperience with perfumes. However I can confirm it certainly does not smell like pencil shavings, I am well familiar with that scent. Perhaps this scent could lean too masculine for some, but I find it too soft to say it would suit most men. That being said, could be a very intriguing and refined fragrance on the right guy.

Overall, if you're a woman that isn't a fan of the obnoxiously sweet or intense floral scents prominent in the world of perfume, in my opinion this is a great perfume to try out, largely due to the accessible price point. On my skin it lasted about 6 hours, and is still lingering! I was careful not to overwhelm my nose with it, so it's possible that if you overspray, it could lead to olfactory fatigue.
If you're looking for an earthy perfume with a soft, elegant twist, it's definitely worth a sniff.

moonstonecoloured 07/03/25 23:03

I tried this fragrance at a perfume meetup and ordered a bottle on the spot — I was completely enchanted.

My love for perfumery began with Dior Bois d’Argent — one of the most beautiful iris scents, where the living iris flower pushes through a haze of cigarette smoke, with none of the powderiness so often found in iris compositions. Here, the flower feels just as alive, but it’s also joined by a few rosebuds, making the fragrance shift like a kaleidoscope — one moment it’s a sultry iris, the next a fragrant rose.
There is a touch of powder here, but it supports the patchouli base — softening it, enriching it.

To me, the bottle and name don’t quite match what I hear in this scent. It feels gothic, dark — something Morticia Addams might wear. A woman who knows her worth, yet whose heart is as delicate as an iris petal.

After a couple of hours, patchouli and rose linger on the skin, staying with you the whole day. Performance 10/10.






MarioKol 06/29/25 03:33

My impressions of the perfume as a man:
Perles de Lalique is not a fragrance you wear casually. From the very first spray, it becomes clear: this is not a playful, sugary scent for girls wrapped in pink ribbons trying to attract attention. No, this is a perfume for women with presence – for women who don’t ask for permission, but make decisions.

The fragrance echoes the philosophy of Chanel: a brand that never created perfumes for carefree girls, but for emancipated women who are firmly rooted in life. Women who have earned their place in the world – with intelligence, style, and elegance. Just like Coco Chanel herself. As a founder and an icon. Coco Chanel would have approved of Perles de Lalique with a nod.

Rose with patchouli, iris, and oakmoss – a composition like a tailored suit. Not a scent for prom night, but for the evening after a successful board meeting. For founders of companies, for managing directors.




illusoryme 05/31/25 11:36

Ghostly elegance. This perfume always reminds me of fog. It doesn’t necessarily smell like the great outdoors, but it has the vibe of a field or a forest shrouded in thick fog during early morning when it’s not yet light out. Maybe because of that, I’m also reminded of the graveyard scene in Silent Hill 2, when James meets Angela. To me, this scent captures the vibe of that environment and conversation. If this were an album, it’d be Faith by The Cure. This is perfect for gloomy, grey, foggy winter days.

I’d describe this scent as damp, powdery, and cold. Rose is prominent in the beginning, and there’s also something minty in here. Patchouli gives this a tiny bit of sweetness. I absolutely love the rose-heavy opening, and I wish the scent stayed like that for its whole lifespan. It fades, however, and I’m left with a subtle woody-patchouli drydown. I feel like I tend to go a little anosmic to this, so I often find myself respraying this throughout the day to be able to smell it again and to relive the pretty rose stage.

Longevity is 3-4 hours. I wish it were better, but I’ve owned my bottle for almost 8 months, and it hasn’t improved yet. Sillage is quite weak – this starts out strong, but becomes very subtle after an hour, even if I sprayed a lot. I often wear this to places where I shouldn’t wear strong perfume, and I also like to spray this on when going to bed, since I find it comforting. This is a skin scent for goths.

Lovaloo 04/19/25 11:32

This one is strange. Not sure about the notes listed above.

Fruity raspberry, black currant, pink pepper in the top. Then a peppery, fruity, green rose alongside a well constructed, dry, papery cedar/papyrus accord. If there is patchouli, it is a construct and doesn't smell very natural. I don't get anything like iris or a realistic oakmoss. As it dries, this perfume rapidly smells like synthetic molecule notes. The base is a peppery, musky cashmeran + iso e super thing, along with some ashy vetiver. It lasts a long time.

The Lalique perfumes are more carefully assembled and usually smell better than other large luxury brands. True to form, Perles de Lalique smells nicer than similar "molecule" releases I've tested, and it's at a great price point if you like this sort of thing. ...However, I can't help but feel a bit disappointed with it. Not a rose centered perfume, and absolutely nothing like Portrait of a Lady, Agent Provocateur, etc.

Folkloric 03/31/25 04:58

Perles is a love at first sniff! I wish I'd discovered it sooner! The patchouli and rose combo in this is so tasteful and addictive! It's a well balanced, mysterious fragrance that makes me think of the many folkloric tales of White Ladies - ghosts of women haunting old castles. It is a beautiful rose and patchouli with earthy yet fresh, cold, spectral notes. I'm so glad that this isn't powdery in an annoying way, or sweet. There is a slight scent of precious incense layered within the prominent rose and patchouli.. But no oriental heaviness to it! It's light as a ghost! Admittedly, I'm at a loss for words to accurately describe this scent. It's such a good, unique and timeless blend imo! It's perfect for folks who like mysterious, unsettling scents, and would like their scent to reflect an effortless spring/summer night goth vibe. Although it's totally wearable all year round. I'm thinking ghosts, moonlight, strings of white pearls and roses on velvety black robes, walking through a private old castle graveyard, reading a book in a rose garden on an overcast day.

As for Perles' supposed similarity to Midnight Poison - I have to say that they do share a similar vibe but only in the late drydown (several hours in). However, while the base bears similarities, Perles leans significantly colder and spectral, while MP remains hypnotizingly sweet in comparison.

Perles is amazing when layered with Encre Noire, for an added dark forest / old church vibe. Also great when layered with Passion de Night (a dupe of Midnight Poison by Dior).

laoganmachilioil 01/09/25 21:00

Let me start off by saying how much I love Lalique's arsenal of flacons. Understated for sure, but Perles' frosted glass bottle edged with the house's signature 'Cactus' dots makes for a hefty and luxurious experience of touch. I expect no less from a house eponymous with high-end glassware, but it never surprises me when such levels of craftsmanship get transcribed upon more 'mass-market' items. Truly a brand for the people!

On to the juice itself, Perles de Lalique firmly represents Nathalie Lorson's utility of Iso E Super at her prime, given that other greats such as Encre Norie were also released along this time. Perles opens up with a nice blast of camphor, backed by a spicy 'Turkish Delight' rose and woody powderiness that persists throughout this fragrance's lifetime post-spray. For a more layman description, I suppose that Perles starts off smelling almost like an old apothecary which gradually fades away into a woody rose.

I largely agree with other sentiments shared by reviewers: Perles is quite a unisex scent, though it does lean slightly feminine and mature. The scent performs beautifully in cooler, more temperate environments, including the savage landscape that is a corporate office; it's distinctive without being offensive. Given its copious dosage of Iso E Super, Perles does last a long time on skin and fabric, although frequent use may lead to gradual anosmia. Overall, it's a signature-worthy fragrance that's worth every dollar. Anyone with an affinity towards Tom Ford's Noir de Noir, woody ouds, or Turkish rose scents should love this as well.

rene.saller 11/04/23 13:20

Blind buy, and so far I have just done a paper test, but I love it so far. A deep, jammy rose, overlaid with pepper and a veritable forest of wood scents. It's sexy but also sort of androgynous. I haven't smelled Femininité du Bois yet, so I can't speak to its similarity (discussed in an excellent Fragrantica appreciation of that perfume, which is how I found out about this one). However, there are aspects of it that remind me of both Rose Flash by Tauerville (a scent I have in rollerball and have adored for years) and also Nirvana Rose by Elizabeth and James, which I also like a great deal. I think the pepper and woods notes might be a trifle more pronounced in the Perles de Lalique (the bottle is insanely elegant, too, especially considering the price of the whole shebang), but it's similar enough to those perfumes that I could see it fulfilling a similar need. To my nose, and at least on paper, the sillage and projection of the PdL are superb and probably superior to the NR and possibly even the RF (although it is unfair to compare a spray to a rollerball, and unfortunately I just have RF as a rollerball, so I can't compare apples to apples, or in this case woody rose chypres to woody rose chypres). Anyway, I'm excited about this one and hope to compare it to other Nathalie Lorson creations once I can do a skin test.

Update: wearing more generally on my skin today. It has a bit of an alarming opening, but it calms down quickly to a beautiful jammy rose with pepper and woods. The iris barely peeks through, but it seems to reinforce the vegetal forest vibe and make it a bit powdery, too (although musks also seem to be prevalent). This is a very elegant and autumnal fragrance, and I like it even more than Le Parfum, my gateway into Lalique fandom.

Update: My husband described the scent as a "fancy pet store," which is what he often says when he smells a prominent cedar note. (At least it isn't a dirty, pee-soaked pet store, lol.) He does like this scent, and I'm going to try to get him to wear it, since to my nose it is extremely unisex, despite the jammy beautiful rose.

To my nose, Perles de Lalique smells more like an enchanted (maybe haunted?) library deep in the forest, a library that's generously stocked with roses and old books, old wooden index cabinets filled with mystical ciphers. The hints of camphor up top confer a bit of an old-timey coughdrop vibe: Maybe the forest librarian has a bit of a cold? The wallpaper looks like rich green velvet, and then you notice that there's oakmoss growing on the walls. In fragrance, as in life, one person's enchanted sylvan library is another person's fancy pet store.

Some Fragranticans describe the woody notes as smelling like pencil shavings, which is something people say whenever they smell cedar or any wood notes at all. As it happens, I have always adored the scent of pencil shavings, so it works out great for me. I'm certain now my enchanted library also has a pencil sharpener, the old-fashioned metal kind that is bolted to the desk. How I loved using those sharpeners in grade school and high school--so satisfying!

Julipet 03/02/23 06:56

Got a tester yesterday and did wrist-to-wrist comparison with Midnight Poison.

With regard to possible MP replacement, it's a similar disappointment to YSL Elle. I can smell no rose. To my nose, it just isn't there, and if Elle at least had some floweriness to it from freesia, Perles de Lalique has none. Other reviewers describe rose and iris, but I'm absolutely anosmic to flowers in this.

At first, there is some patchouli, making it herbal, bitter, and medicinal, but then it fades away and only pepper stays for hours, slowly morphing into warm woodiness and something salty.

MP and Lalique do go through one similar note as they develop - something evil, earthy, poisonous - but it sounds so different in MP and Lalique. In MP it smells moist like dirt and moss under a rosebush, while in Perles it's very dry and lifeless, like dust on a glass apothecary cabinet where herbariums are kept.

The bottle and the box design is spot on. The scent is white, dry, minimalistic. Perles de Lalique paints to my mind a picture of stern beauty - a shining desert flooded with light. I cannot quite decide whether it's an icy desert, desiccated by bitter frost, or a sun-bleached dune desert. In my YSL Elle review earlier I compared MP to Maleficent and Elle to Cruella. In that case, Perles de Lalique is definitely the White Witch-Queen of Narnia and the spiciness is from that half-Jinn side of hers.

I'd say this scent is androgynous. Maybe more feminine, but overall too ethereal to have a defined gender. It is beautiful and sophisticated, but it's not the energy that vibes with me.

UPD: Came back to tell that after a couple of days in the closet, my sweatshirt does give off that familiar Midnight Poison residual smell. Bravo, Perles de Lalique,10 points for longevity! I didn’t even spray it on my clothes, the scent rubbed off from the skin. However, it’s only a ghost of Midnight Poison. I now understand why people compare the two, but similarity isn’t nearly enough for me to see Perles as a replacement.
I also must admit that in warmer weather and when worn on its own, without comparison to MP, rose in PDL is more pronounced (well, DETECTABLE, at least). Still, it’s a very dry, salty, desert rose.

Subhuman 02/01/22 20:22

Elegant and electric. And further proof that Fragrantica's note listings are suggested reading only, because on my skin this thing has a honking, Tauer-sized incense that nearly tramples the rose. It gives Perles a surprisingly bohemian streak, like a rich woman who was once a tarot reader. The heart of the scent is a rosy, patchouli-dusted "modern chypre" accord, but Perles avoids falling in with that generally lazy group thanks to quality ingredients and an expert craftsman at the helm. The rose is juicy and plush, the patchouli smells properly peppery and natural, and the incense, vetiver, and a translucent cedar (Iso E Super) keep things crisp. It's all so chic, and so perfectly modulated, that for a moment you might wonder whether the glory days of the chypre are gone after all. The form is different, but the spirit seems intact. Somehow Lalique fragrances are still a steal on discount sites at a time when just about every cheap thrill is reaching above its station, so if you're at all inclined toward sheer, rosey-woody-incensey things with equal parts pizzazz and pure breeding, Perles de Lalique should be on your list.

Nathalie Lorson created in 2006 for the Lalique brand a jewel that is rarely talked about, this essence that should be labeled unisex was launched as feminine and although it can perfectly be used by a woman, she must have character and personality to wear it because it pulls a little towards the masculine side, this beautiful fragrance It has made the note of rose grow in me to the point of dazzling me.
Perles is a perfume of contrasts and although it is not challenging I think it could not be to everyone's liking, this fragrance opens with a rose note, cold and austere, slightly powdery and spicy due to pepper and iris, this opening in rare and somewhat wet (I guess because of the vetiver) and mutates minutes later into a bomb of dry patchouli, camphorated with cool traces that adheres to the rose and creates a wonderful combination that remains present throughout the duration of the fragrance, this combo of rose and camphorated patchouli may remind you the wonderful and sadly discontinued Midnight Poison by Dior but here it doesn't go down a dark path and there are no traces of sweetness anywhere, this composition goes from wet to dry in minutes, it's very white and cold but immensely enjoyable, already in the drydown we find a cashmirwood and Iso E super that give it a tone between woody and earthy.
This fragrance makes a perfect chemistry with my skin, I have tried it both in extreme heat and in cooler climates and it always works for me, it has a moderate projection although it is perfectly perceived and lasts well, a jewel of pure olfactory experience that I recommend although I know is not to everyone's taste.

peppered patchouli

smora 06/11/20 11:47

Iso E Chypre (Nathalie Lorson, 2006)

Scentrack: Ella Fitzgerald – Wait 'Till You See Him (De-Phazz Remix)

The fragrance itself is 21st century floral Chypre. The floral heart of every classical Chypre (rose and jasmine) is introduced in contemporary woody-spicy environment. Very soft and wet rose, pepper, slightly powdery iris and jasmine are put in powerful, but transparent cocoon of Iso E Super. Iso E Super gives a strong touch of bright woods to this fragrance, but it is not flat and boring due to the sparkling aspects of rose a jasmine. According to Ohloff G et al.* Perles de Lalique contains the molecule Paradisone (enantiomerically pure Hedione) with jasmine odor and an amazing 80% of the Iso E Super molecule! The base is very soft, containing mild patchouli and Chypre-characteristic strong musky notes.
Rose, jasmine and musk give some classic feeling around this fragrance, while pepper and lots of Iso E Super ultra-contemporary touch, resulting in pronounced and balanced duality. High dose of Iso E Super is the reason of the unisex character of Perles de Lalique, but I really admire the hidden female sensuality of this beautiful fragrance. Clean, easy to wear, refined, sensual and lovely Lalique’s treasure.

*Ohloff G, Pickenhagen W, Kraft P. Scent and Chemistry: The Molecular World of Odors. Wiley-VCH, Zurich, 2012.

Rating: 8.5/10

Juliana6 06/29/15 13:28

I really appreciate the perfumes of Lalique, because they are unique,individualistic, very special, they are not supposed to please the crowd or directly follow the trends, and this one is like that too.
Perles de Lalique is the perfume for a special mood. I wear it when I want to spend some time just with myself alone. Sometimes I don't want to see anybody, to talk, to smile, to be sociable, some kind of a restart. A noble perfume (and for that reason not always understood correctly), a unique one. It can be compared with "Femme Individuelle" by Mont Blanc - the same juniper, pepper and rose vibe.
This perfume for me is a wild juniper wood near the sea, a meadow where the wild roses and some tiny violets grow, a warm summer day without the sun, the dark clouds, the wind becoming stronger and stronger, blowing through the high pines and juniper branches, some drops of rain falling in my hands like the real pearls. Like the breath of the nature. The freedom and the sincerity.

puddley 01/12/14 13:00

As a fragrance blogger and ardent fumie, I get to smell a lot of high end niche perfumery. More recently, I seem to be turning back to more mainstream and designer scents because of the quality and innovation that is happening in those places that we turned our noses up at - the department store!

I smelt Perles in Selfridges this weekend after a bore-fest at the 'wall of niche' where no new releases and no samples appeared. This perfume flabbergasted me.

Perles is awash with ISO E Super (the velveteen woody aroma-chemical that was responsible for the popularity of Ecsentric Molecules 1). Apparently it contains 80% of it (albeit in dilution of course). The notes read as a standard patchouli chypre, but what you can't perceive from the notes is it's vibrancy. It has an aldehyde-like uplifting brightness that feels immensely euphoric. It reminded me of a less rosy, more woody, version of one of my all time favourites - Calypso by Robert Piguet. The patchouli is there (especially towards the drydown), but it's not overpoweringly patchouli. This stuff has subtly and a great transformation from the peppery bright beginning through to a soft whisper of a woodsy close. It has impressive longevity too.

I would say that this is not 'for women' but unisex. I would also say that it's flipping marvellous!

rene.saller 11/04/23 13:20

Blind buy, and so far I have just done a paper test, but I love it so far. A deep, jammy rose, overlaid with pepper and a veritable forest of wood scents. It's sexy but also sort of androgynous. I haven't smelled Femininité du Bois yet, so I can't speak to its similarity (discussed in an excellent Fragrantica appreciation of that perfume, which is how I found out about this one). However, there are aspects of it that remind me of both Rose Flash by Tauerville (a scent I have in rollerball and have adored for years) and also Nirvana Rose by Elizabeth and James, which I also like a great deal. I think the pepper and woods notes might be a trifle more pronounced in the Perles de Lalique (the bottle is insanely elegant, too, especially considering the price of the whole shebang), but it's similar enough to those perfumes that I could see it fulfilling a similar need. To my nose, and at least on paper, the sillage and projection of the PdL are superb and probably superior to the NR and possibly even the RF (although it is unfair to compare a spray to a rollerball, and unfortunately I just have RF as a rollerball, so I can't compare apples to apples, or in this case woody rose chypres to woody rose chypres). Anyway, I'm excited about this one and hope to compare it to other Nathalie Lorson creations once I can do a skin test.

Update: wearing more generally on my skin today. It has a bit of an alarming opening, but it calms down quickly to a beautiful jammy rose with pepper and woods. The iris barely peeks through, but it seems to reinforce the vegetal forest vibe and make it a bit powdery, too (although musks also seem to be prevalent). This is a very elegant and autumnal fragrance, and I like it even more than Le Parfum, my gateway into Lalique fandom.

Update: My husband described the scent as a "fancy pet store," which is what he often says when he smells a prominent cedar note. (At least it isn't a dirty, pee-soaked pet store, lol.) He does like this scent, and I'm going to try to get him to wear it, since to my nose it is extremely unisex, despite the jammy beautiful rose.

To my nose, Perles de Lalique smells more like an enchanted (maybe haunted?) library deep in the forest, a library that's generously stocked with roses and old books, old wooden index cabinets filled with mystical ciphers. The hints of camphor up top confer a bit of an old-timey coughdrop vibe: Maybe the forest librarian has a bit of a cold? The wallpaper looks like rich green velvet, and then you notice that there's oakmoss growing on the walls. In fragrance, as in life, one person's enchanted sylvan library is another person's fancy pet store.

Some Fragranticans describe the woody notes as smelling like pencil shavings, which is something people say whenever they smell cedar or any wood notes at all. As it happens, I have always adored the scent of pencil shavings, so it works out great for me. I'm certain now my enchanted library also has a pencil sharpener, the old-fashioned metal kind that is bolted to the desk. How I loved using those sharpeners in grade school and high school--so satisfying!

catswearingperfume 09/23/20 13:41

A modern woody rose in a classic, earthy chypre. The opening is sharp, medicinal, herbal - bay leaf, maybe? Whatever it is, it is intentional and it surprised me. I couldn't decide if I liked it, and as I was contemplating, it faded slightly to make room for the rose and the wood notes. Enough of that herbal note sticks around to add earthiness throughout this progression.

The patchouli in this is very clean, but I detect another wood element that smells strongly of cedar. The rose is cold, present, but never fully takes over the composition. The dry down is mostly wood. The whole experience is cold, serious, stoic. Austere, even.


EDIT: Wearing this again and there is definitely a very long phase in this fragrance that smells like cedar shavings for a hamster cage. I like wood accords, but not like this. This fragrance is sadly not for me.

zosoroxy 03/21/15 23:42

Negative review, written with utmost r-e-s-p-e-c-t, & sincerest apologies, to all the more sophisticated, experienced perfumistas/misters, whom enjoy this quite well regarded perfume. This 'fume stands the test of time, so it obviously takes a more well-trained, sensory experienced nose than I, to "get" this frag.

Based upon my limited experience, I've learned that I dig peppered/spiced 'fumes, where the spices accent (or are juxtaposed against) all manner of rich & delicate florals, woods, moss, bright citrus & alternate succulent fruits- iow, all traditional perfume compositional notes. (I especially love zingy, tender young ginger essence).

Sadly, however, my inexperienced olfaction translates Perles Lalique as overwhelmingly bone-dry, dusty, supermarket-shelf quality, stale, powdered peppercorns. There does seem to be a secret floral accord hidden within, but it only ever hinted & peeked out from underneath the predominant stale powdered pepper, which was so strong I couldn't escape tasting & choking on it, in the back of my throat.

I hold greatest esteem for those whom enjoy this (or any) perfume favorites. Again, I'm sorry so write so negatively... Please bear in mind that this was just my own subjective experience w/ a sample of the EdP. (So I encourage others to take my personal pepper sensitivity with a grain of salt, lol!) I tried (really!), waiting it out, for the heartnotes to emerge- But after 2 hours of throat & nasal passages irritation, I thought "Perfume is subjective. Life is too short to force myself to endure this obvious non-like, just because I want to be a cool perfumista." - And I scrubbed it off. Perhaps with more time, experience, & education in the fine art of perfumery, I'll be able to better appreciate this much admired staple (?) Keeping an open mind, but at the same time, learning to just trust my own likes/dislikes.

Upsides- Beautiful, unique bottle, unigender, affordable, & (probable) great sillage & longevity.

perfumeaddiction 05/20/14 21:48

Ladies and Gentleman this is all about the Patchouli! Quite dry and spicy. Out of the bottle it was not appealing to me. On my wrist the fragrance transforms into a lovely warm scent. Honestly I am not getting any form of rose here. This one is bold and strong. If your not a patch fan avoid this one at all costs as it will not be your friend. It has a unisex vibe but then again to me all patchouli scents seem to go both ways. It is very easy to become asnomic this scent so be cautious. It's there you just can't smell it. I am wearing this one side by side to YSL Elle. While the two are sisters they are not identical twins. Elle has a touch more sweet cedar femininity while Perles is a more dry Patchouli. If I had to pick between the two I would go with Elle over Perles yet if your an Elle fan and can't find it at a good cost grab Perles. This is definitely not your common mainstream smelling scent which I do like in a perfume. Ideal for the cooler months. Elle smells fresh cedar and I get a clean yet dirty scent with Perles. This is not a put off by any means yet I would have to be in the mood to wear it and for me that would not be every day.
